name: FastDB
tagline: Knizhnik's main-memory object-relational database for C++, mapping the whole database into process memory.
description: FastDB is an embedded main-memory object-relational database by Konstantin Knizhnik, first released in January 1999. It maps the entire database file into the application's address space with the OS virtual-memory system, so records are read in place with no buffer manager or copying, and tables are declared directly from C++ classes. It provides an SQL-like query language with object extensions (references, arrays, inverse references), T-tree, hash and R-tree indexes, transactions committed through a shadow-page scheme with no write-ahead log, near-instant recovery, online backup and replication for fault tolerance, plus C, C++, Delphi/Kylix and PHP interfaces. It is fast for datasets that fit in RAM; GigaBASE was its disk-based sibling. The last version, 3.76, came out in May 2014.
statusNote: Last release 3.76 (May 2014); the author has since moved on to PostgreSQL work. Consider SQLite, LMDB or eXtremeDB for embedded in-memory use.

scale.notes: Whole database must fit in the process address space and RAM; replication provides hot standby, not scale-out.

queryLanguages: SQL-like query language with object extensions
strengths: Zero-copy reads: data is accessed directly in memory-mapped pages
Log-less shadow-page commits with near-instant crash recovery
C++ classes double as table definitions, with automatic schema evolution
R-tree, T-tree and hash indexes in a tiny embeddable library
weaknesses: Database size limited by RAM and address space
No release since 2014; old build systems and compilers
Single-machine embedded use; no standard SQL or network protocol
useCases: Low-latency embedded data in C++ applications (telecom, real-time systems)
